review: 3:1–3:4 — the Arabic's drought imagery (no rain, grass and fruit gone) is Habakkuk 3:17, where the same list of losses is answered by rejoicing in the Lord; Hebrew keeps the sequence because the next stanza quotes the answer.
4:1–4:2 לֹא־חָדַל / בַּאדֹנָי יִשְׂמָח — 'has not ceased to rejoice in the Lord'; חָדַל is the biblical verb for ceasing (1 Sam 12:23), used so the line stays at seven.
4:3–4:4 וְגַם־לְשׁוֹנִי תּוֹדֶה / אֲהַלְּלָה אוֹתוֹ — the Arabic has 'my tongue too, thanking, praises Him'; Hebrew splits the two verbs across the lines, as the tune's caesura does.
1:3–1:4 וּמִי יֶאֱהַב לִבִּי — the Arabic يَا تُرَى ('I wonder') marks the question; Hebrew drops the particle because the interrogative מִי already carries it and the line needs the syllable.
